newsitem.title: UK: EU planner warns of new farm surpluses.
newsitem.headline: EU planner warns of new farm surpluses.

text.p: There is a high risk that EU stocks of the main agricultural products will pile up again, once the ten planned new members in central and eastern Europe take their place, according to an EU official.

Dirk Ahner, head of the director general's policy unit in the EU Commission's Agriculture Directorate said "To be clear, we do not expect, as has been predicted, that there will be a rapid explosion of production and surpluses in the new countries."

"In fact there are still too many structural handicaps in the agricultural economies, but also in the upstream and downstream sectors linked to agriculture which these countries will have to overcome first," he said in a speech to the Oxford Farming Conference.
Ahner estimated the extra farm spending at 12 to 13 billion ECU by the end of the first decade of the next century, if all ten candidates accede to the EU in the first year of the decade.

The combination of the pressure from new members and likely extra limits on EU exports, as another round of world trade talks puts a new cap on export subsidies, would oblige the EU to impose an arable set-aside rate 25-26 per cent, according to Ahner's calculations.
There would also need to be cuts in dairy quotas and increased regulation in the beef sector.
"In all cases, our share in world trade would diminish sharply," he said. "Is this the way we want to go?"
The creation of more jobs and income sources outside agriculture was, therefore, a major challenge for rural development policy in Europe.
